questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find out the age of a very old tree
Why forests are dying because of coronavirus
How insects and caterpillars choose what to eat
Whether trees can remember stress
questions.why: Sam says they'll ask whether trees can remember, and if so, whether it helps them fight disease.

questions.q: According to Neil, what does the human body do with stressful past experiences?
options: It forgets them completely after a few years
It stores them in our genes and passes them on
It keeps them only in the blood
It removes them while we sleep
questions.why: He says our body stores stressful situations in our genes and passes the information to our children.

questions.q: How does Sam first react to the idea of trees having memories?
options: She doubts it
She's excited by it
She already knew it
She finds it scary
questions.why: Sam says, 'But surely trees don't have memories, Neil!'

questions.q: What does Neil suggest could be a kind of memory in trees?
options: The colour of their leaves
The height of their branches
The rings they grow each year
The smell of their flowers
questions.why: He says trees grow a ring for each year of growth, and 'that could be a kind of memory'.

questions.q: According to Jurriaan Ton, why do plants need a very good immune system?
options: They grow much more slowly than animals
They have no leaves in the winter months
They need a lot of water to survive
Many things eat them, and they can't escape
questions.why: He says plants sit at the bottom of the food chain and are rooted to the ground, so can't escape.

questions.q: What example of stress for a tree does Neil give?
options: Not getting enough water
Being moved to a new place
Having too many birds on it
Growing too close to a house
questions.why: Neil says for trees stress is more basic, 'something like not getting enough water'.

questions.q: According to Dr Estrella Luna-Diez, what does a small tree ring show?
options: The tree was very healthy that year
The tree had some kind of stress that year
The tree was cut by people that year
The tree produced a lot of fruit that year
questions.why: Sam says a small ring shows the tree didn't grow much that year, which indicates some outside stress.

questions.q: What is Dr Luna-Diez's idea about how long trees remember stress?
options: They remember every dry month for their whole life
They never remember any stress at all
Long droughts may stay; a dry month fades
They only remember stress when they are young
questions.why: She suggests a long drought may be remembered for a long time, but a dry July may be forgotten within a year.
